items.title: architecture: Close Planning DB component evidence gaps

labels.name: priority: medium
labels.description: Medium priority - important but not blocking

items.body:
## Problem
`pnpm planning:db:integrity:check` currently reports 53 `component_evidence_gap` warnings from `planning_query_store.component_engineering_component_tree_query`. The affected Planning DB components are marked `incomplete` because their profiles do not connect the expected engineering evidence categories: tests, documentation, public API, invariants, transitions, and consumers.

This is not 53 independent product defects. It is a component-engineering evidence coverage gap across the component tree. Fifteen components currently have evidence count `0`; the remaining components have partial evidence but still fail the completeness rule. Inventory command:

```text
pnpm planning:db:query component-integrity --limit 500
```

The warning passes only because the progressive baseline allows 53 findings. The baseline must not become permanent authority for incomplete profiles.

## Governing sources

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/planning/status/governance-document-rule-inventory.md`
- `docs/architecture/components/ci-governance/component-engineering-invariants.md`
- `docs/architecture/components/ci-governance/component-engineering-record-component.md`
- `ADR-0061` (Planning DB owns components, evidence, and architecture)

## Proposed solution

Complete the component-engineering evidence model at the source rather than suppressing the warning:

1. Export the 53 rows with component ID, evidence count, source path, and expected evidence categories.
2. For each component, identify canonical source files and existing tests/docs/contracts/architecture tests; do not invent duplicate documents or task trackers.
3. Add or correct Planning DB component evidence relations through the existing import/operation rail.
4. Where a component is only a grouping/root component, define the minimum valid evidence profile explicitly instead of forcing irrelevant product evidence.
5. Add a deterministic query/test proving evidence completeness for every governed component.
6. Reduce the progressive baseline from 53 to the residual count, then drive it to zero through follow-up work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pnpm planning:db:query component-integrity --limit 500` reports no unexpected `component_evidence_gap` rows for complete profiles.
- The 15 zero-evidence components have an explicit disposition: wired evidence, valid grouping profile, or separately governed retirement/reclassification.
- Evidence relations resolve to canonical repository paths and do not create parallel architecture authority.
- Component-engineering tests cover a complete profile, a valid grouping/root profile, and an incomplete profile.
- `pnpm planning:db:integrity:check --strict` passes without a progressive-baseline regression.
- Validation evidence is recorded in this issue and the implementation PR.

## Out of scope

- Creating a local workboard or Planning DB task rows.
- Reclassifying components solely to make the warning disappear.
- Duplicating documentation already owned by #3642.
- Relaxing the integrity query or warning budget.

items.body:
## Outcome / DoR

User approved a compact left activity rail with Sources and Elements for the main Canvas, sharing presentation with the semantic editor. Best-effort implementation, no new product semantics, providers, contracts or persistence.

## Current state and rationale

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Main[Main Canvas] --> Graph[Graph and contextual menus]
  Semantic[Semantic editor] --> Catalogue[Fixed Sources catalogue with separate collapse icon]
  Catalogue --> Existing[Existing source occurrence commands]
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Main[Main Canvas adapter] --> Explorer[Shared left rail and resizable panel]
  Semantic[Semantic editor adapter] --> Explorer
  Explorer --> Sources[Sources content owned by each context]
  Explorer --> Elements[Existing elements: select and locate, never duplicate]
  Explorer --> Surface[Retained graph surface]
```

One visible panel at a time; activating it again collapses it. Keep search, selection and graph mounted. No automatic graph fit on toggle. Existing graph focus and import ports remain authoritative. Sources in the main Canvas are the already imported source nodes plus the existing import action; the semantic catalogue continues to add source occurrences. No invented global source catalogue.

## Governance and rails

AGENTS.md; governance-document-rule-inventory.md; command-query-rail-governance.md; fowler-opportunity-planning-governance.md; ai-work-protocol.md. Reuse RenderCanvasContextualGraphSurface (query, CanvasAuthoringPresentation), InspectCanvasNode/ProjectCanvasRelationalTree and existing source import / ConfigureCanvasDvtNode actions. No new write rail or domain policy. Current authorized workspace/model only; read-only navigation remains available, writes keep existing guards.

## Fowler / conformity matrix

| Scenario | Opportunity | Fowler pattern | DDD owner | Command/query rail | Implementation surfaces | Unit or package test | Architecture test | User-flow test | Out of scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Open/change/collapse left panel | Duplicate presentation | Extract Component, composition | CanvasAuthoringPresentation | RenderCanvasContextualGraphSurface | Canvas explorer frame, template, CSS, copy; main/semantic composition | Preserve child state, keyboard labels, toggle | No domain/store/network imports in frame | Existing Canvas navigation flow extended | New global layout framework |
| Find existing elements | Hidden identity risk | Read-model projection + existing command ports | Canvas graph / semantic relation | Existing render/inspection rails | Main and semantic explorer adapters | Stable IDs, duplicate labels, read-only, empty/search | No graph mutation in projection | Select existing item without increasing count | New duplication commands, new backend queries |

## DoD

### User correction: imported sources and window lifecycle

The new navigation filter incorrectly assumed `role: source`; the canonical graph uses `role: input`. Consume that role without provider-specific branching. A live graph update must populate Sources without remounting the explorer.

```mermaid
stateDiagram-v2
  Open --> Collapsed: Collapse button or active rail button
  Collapsed --> Open: Sources or Elements rail button
  Open --> Closed: Close explorer
  Collapsed --> Closed: View menu
  Closed --> Open: View / Canvas explorer
```

Collapse keeps the activity rail; Close hides the rail and panel until explicitly restored from View. Reuse existing UiLayoutState visual preferences for the persisted visibility flag, while each explorer retains its own search and active tab. Preserve graph identity and width. No new graph command or automatic imports/selection. Add localized collapse/close actions, keyboard and browser proof; invalid persisted visibility defaults to visible. Existing `RenderCanvasContextualGraphSurface` remains the owning query, with `UiLayoutState` as UI preference owner.

- Sources/Elements rail, consistent SVG icons, active indicator, accessible names and keyboard interaction.
- Resizable dock, no modal; same frame in main and semantic surfaces.
- Localized ES/EN text; templates and CSS modules separate from adapters.
- No graph/draft mutation on tab changes, search or selection; no source recreation.

- Focused tests red/green, web lint/typecheck, ARC evaluation and verify:prepush; report any blocked checks accurately.
- No stubs, new debt, relaxed rules or bypassed hooks.

## Delivery

One implementation branch and scoped commits. No changes to unrelated CI/Transform investigation. Integration only after the required gates pass.

## Approved behavior correction: registration is not placement

User explicitly confirmed: importing only registers the source in the left catalogue; clicking inspects configuration; only a drop places a card. Existing cards must not be removed.

Current: ImportSourceObjects -> semantic nodes + visible nodeIds + positions -> automatic focus. Save filters semantic nodes by visible IDs. Clicking the semantic catalogue may also add occurrences.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Import[ImportSourceObjects] --> Catalogue[Persisted semantic source catalogue]
  Catalogue -->|click| Inspect[InspectCanvasNode configuration]
  Catalogue -->|drop| Place[CreateCanvasNode admission]
  Place --> Visible[Visible nodeIds and positions]
  Catalogue --> Save[SaveWorkspaceGraphDraft]
  Visible --> Save
  Visible --> Execute[Preview / Plan / Run scope]
```

Reuse the v1 graph contract: nodes are declared semantics, nodeIds are placed identities, nodePositions belongs exactly to nodeIds. No CSS-hidden cards, local-only catalogue, schema migration or new provider coupling. Existing node admission is idempotent for the same graph identity; semantic source occurrences remain separately identified. Do not invent a duplicate graph-creation rail.

| Scenario | Opportunity | Pattern | DDD owner | Rail | Allowed surfaces | Test | Architecture guard | User-flow | Out of scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Import without a card | Mixed command responsibilities | Separate registration from placement | SourceImportRequest / WorkspaceGraphAuthoringDraft | ImportSourceObjects | API graph draft import + web completion | Preserved topology, idempotency, inactive canvas, conflict rollback | Import completion does not admit/focus nodes | Import then reload | Provider discovery changes |
| Inspect and place registered source | Hidden visibility authority | Read model and explicit command | Canvas graph and inspector | InspectCanvasNode / CreateCanvasNode | Graph projection, explorer adapter, inspector selection, existing drop admission | Click does not mutate; drop keeps permissions and duplicate admission | Presentation delegates existing ports | Click, cancel drag, drop | New provider or model semantics |
| Save catalogue without placing it | Data loss from visibility filtering | Aggregate persistence | WorkspaceGraphAuthoringDraft | SaveWorkspaceGraphDraft | Draft serialization / lifecycle / source edits | Save and reload retain unplaced sources; edits do not reveal source | Execution scope remains visible IDs | Reload after source configuration | Bulk reset of existing data |

items.title: architecture: Map implemented components to canonical authority

labels.name: priority: medium
labels.description: Medium priority - important but not blocking

items.body:
## Problem
`pnpm planning:db:integrity:check` currently reports 54 `component_missing_architecture_authority` warnings. The affected components are implemented, but their Planning DB records are `unplanned` and have no canonical architecture authority relation. The source view identifies the generated index path as:

```text
.generated-docs/planning/status/system-governance-component-index.components.yaml
```

This is an authority mapping gap, not proof that the corresponding code does not exist. Each component needs an explicit link to an accepted design identity, ADR, governed component document, or other Planning DB-backed architecture evidence. Inventory commands:

```text
pnpm planning:db:query component-integrity --limit 500
pnpm planning:db:query component-roadmap --limit 500
```

The warning passes only because the progressive baseline allows 54 findings. That baseline must not substitute for architecture ownership.

## Governing sources

- `AGENTS.md`
- `docs/planning/status/governance-document-rule-inventory.md`
- `docs/architecture/command-query-rail-governance.md`
- `docs/architecture/components/ci-governance/component-engineering-record-component.md`
- `ADR-0061` (Planning DB owns components, relations, ownership, and architecture evidence)
- Planning DB `architecture-designs` authority query

## Proposed solution

Build a canonical component-to-architecture-authority reconciliation:

1. Export all 54 affected component IDs and names.
2. Match each component to an existing Planning DB architecture design, accepted ADR, canonical component document, or governed evidence path.
3. Reuse existing authority identities; do not create synonyms or a second architecture catalog.
4. For components with no legitimate architecture authority, classify them explicitly as grouping/operational metadata and define the supported authority posture, or retire/reclassify them through the existing Planning DB mechanism.
5. Make the generated component index consume the canonical relation rather than infer authority from filesystem presence.
6. Add an integrity test preventing an implemented component from remaining `unplanned` without an explicit approved exception.
7. Reduce the progressive baseline from 54 to the residual count and then remove the residual through follow-up work.

## Acceptance criteria

- `pnpm planning:db:query component-integrity --limit 500` reports no unexpected `component_missing_architecture_authority` rows.
- Every affected component has exactly one canonical authority posture: linked design/ADR/evidence, explicitly valid grouping component, or governed retirement/reclassification.
- No duplicate architecture authority, local task tracker, or parallel document index is introduced.
- The generated component index and Planning DB query agree on authority state.
- `pnpm planning:db:integrity:check --strict` passes without a progressive-baseline regression.
- Validation evidence and residual exceptions are recorded in this issue and the implementation PR.

## Out of scope

- Replacing Planning DB with generated Markdown.
- Creating one new ADR per component without a durable decision.
- Treating issue status as architecture authority.
- Suppressing the warning or increasing the baseline.

items.title: TASK-ENG1.3 Model unknown provider outcomes and make reconciliation and compensation safe
items.body:
## Plan vigente — redispatch condicionado a evidencia

Parent: #2673. Coordinación y autoridad de ownership: #2678.

**Orientación aprobada expresamente por Dunay:** conservar la base segura de ownership/observación y permitir redispatch de aplicación únicamente bajo un perfil de Temporal cuya garantía esté demostrada. Sin evidencia suficiente, mantener `unknown -> observe -> backoff -> escalate`.

La aprobación confirma la propuesta de trabajo; **no certifica la garantía del provider, no habilita redispatch, no autoriza una integración sin sus gates y no elimina la aceptación positiva pendiente de esta issue**. Se conserva la prioridad P0.

Investigación, fuentes primarias, alternativas y matriz detallada: [ENG1.3-REDISPATCH-STUDY-R1](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/2679#issuecomment-5926921272). Ese estudio conserva su baseline histórico; este cuerpo consolida la dirección aprobada y el estado de entrega vigente. Sustituye las propuestas anteriores que equiparaban un Workflow ID determinista con garantía ilimitada, o planteaban cerrar la aceptación de redispatch únicamente con observación/escalado.

## Estado reconciliado y evidencia reutilizada

Actualización administrativa contrastada con GitHub; `main` observado: `3d580cb71ffad58b462b827f145d51d1552494d3`. Esta actualización no reejecuta suites ni certifica de nuevo todo ese HEAD.

| Parte | Entrega comprobada | Pendiente / límite |
|---|---|---|
| Ownership y fencing | #2678 está CLOSED/completed. #3506 integrada en `3991aac9809ac92292984c17992737c72e9af9fa`, head revisado `029c14dc165198be23bea48b29a5bec9d6f10022`. | Reutilizar; no reimplementar claim, stores, API recovery ni reconciliador. Integración no equivale a despliegue sobre una base existente. |
| Incertidumbre, observación y compensación | #3506 aporta unknown durable antes del RPC, escrituras cercadas, observación tipada, compensación al execution ID observado y backoff/escalado. | La base integrada no realiza redispatch automático de aplicación. |
| Evidencia de deduplicación Temporal | #3507 integrada en `26d86c60aaf1429eb31030515a7a18dfd9247cde`, head `686f10bb307029b35f0ea8acc9d08c746ab48232`. | Tres pruebas reales de órdenes de llegada controlados y pérdida de identidad. No acreditan una cota de decisión remota, fallos arbitrarios de red, expiración natural, HA/restore, binding inmutable completo ni la vertical automática. |
| Perfil admisible y redispatch seguro | Dirección de estudio/implementación aprobada en esta issue. | **NO ADMITIDO / NO HABILITADO.** Faltan la prueba temporal y operativa, el binding y la aceptación integral. |

El bloqueo ya no es la ausencia de #2678: es la **admisión demostrada del perfil de redispatch y su implementación/aceptación**. No retirar `status:blocked` por interpretar estas pruebas parciales como capacidad entregada.

Evidencias de integración: [#3506](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/2679#issuecomment-5927344942), [#3507](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/2679#issuecomment-5929477346). No se vuelven a atribuir a `main` los antiguos fallos catch-to-null o policies retiradas descritos en el diagnóstico de septiembre; quedan como antecedentes de las correcciones enlazadas.

## Invariante de producto

> Timeout local, interrupción de transporte, lectura fallida, cancelación aceptada o un `missing` puntual no demuestran que una ejecución nunca existió, no pueda materializarse tarde o esté compensada.

Conservar separadas las autoridades de:

```text
ownership / autorización de cada intento
estado canónico del run
conocimiento de la ejecución del provider
compensación
programación de reconciliación / escalado
```

Separar también tres garantías: una autoridad lógica en DVT; ausencia de una segunda cadena independiente por retransmitir su inicio; e idempotencia de los efectos externos de Activities. Probar una no prueba automáticamente las otras. Safe redispatch aporta disponibilidad/recuperación y sigue siendo una aceptación pendiente, no una optimización eliminada del alcance.

## Reglas base que el siguiente corte debe preservar

1. El receipt vigente es obligatorio para autorización y escrituras owner-driven. El fencing se comprueba dentro de la transacción que protege la mutación canónica; no vale leer ownership y escribir después sin protección.
2. Persistir `unknown/start_requested` antes del RPC. Un error ambiguo o fallo al persistir la respuesta no se convierte en ausencia ni fallo canónico definitivo.
3. Mantener `found | missing_at_observation | failed | unsupported` diferenciados. Un error de lectura nunca equivale a `null/missing` ni autoriza efectos sobre el provider.
4. Adoptar sólo observaciones positivas vinculadas al intento lógico y compatibles con el estado canónico. Canonical terminal no adopta un provider activo; compensación requerida no vuelve a adopción.
5. `cancel()` aceptado no confirma compensación. Cancelar el execution ID exacto observado; observar después. Completed/failed/timed-out huérfano no se presenta como cancelado; se escala cuando no hay resultado canónico compatible.
6. Un receipt obsoleto no autoriza nuevos envíos, escrituras ni cancelaciones. Reclaim no retira un RPC previamente autorizado/en tránsito: su llegada tardía debe estar cubierta por la garantía remota y la identidad original.
7. Unknown y compensación pendientes sobreviven restart y siguen seleccionables con orden estable, batch acotado, próximo vencimiento y backoff reproducible/capado. Escalado es durable, consultable y no equivale a resolved ni produce hot polling.
8. Recovery API no informa confirmed/accepted por mera existencia de metadata mientras haya incertidumbre, compensación o escalado incompatibles.
9. Una conclusión definitiva requiere evidencia positiva suficiente y produce como máximo un evento canónico apropiado con identidad idempotente. `missing` puntual tras autorización no habilita `RunFailed`, expiry ni redispatch.
10. Reutilizar el aggregate de intent, stores, adapter y mantenimiento existentes. Sin segundo scheduler, worker, tabla de leases, provider-state store, registry paralelo ni aliases ID-only.

## Política aprobada de redispatch

### Dos modos condicionados a evidencia

```text
observation_only(reason)
  o
bounded_redispatch(identityBinding, firstAuthorizedAt, notAfter, evidenceRevision)
```

Son nombres conceptuales del diseño, no un nuevo DTO o puerto ya admitido. No usar un simple `supportsRetry: true`.

Distinguir los retries de transporte del SDK dentro de una llamada y un nuevo envío de aplicación por mantenimiento. Ambos consumen el horizonte/presupuesto total; no se desactivan los retries SDK indiscriminadamente ni se multiplican bucles de retry.

### Identidad y autoridad del reenvío

- Mismo namespace/identidad de despliegue, Workflow ID, tenant e intento lógico. Una ejecución nueva pedida por el usuario no es este redispatch.
- Mismo contenido semántico del inicio: PlanRef/hash, contexto inmutable, tipo de workflow, parámetros y políticas relevantes. No regenerar silenciosamente un request distinto desde configuración posterior a un despliegue.
- Receipt vigente y autorización durable atómica de cada envío permitido; presupuesto registrado en el mismo intent.
- Ninguna conclusión definitiva, cancelación solicitada, compensación pendiente/confirmada ni decisión canónica incompatible.
- Política remota `FAIL + REJECT_DUPLICATE`. Ante `AlreadyStarted`, observar/verificar el vínculo; no asumir éxito, fabricar un fallo ni cancelar al supuesto ganador.
- Un `requestId` persistido no sustituye retención, binding ni fencing. No utilizar APIs internas del SDK. Sólo evaluar el API público de bajo nivel dentro del adapter si aporta una garantía demostrada, preservando codecs, headers, tracing y clasificación de errores.
- Medir convergencia de la cadena lógica; no confundir un cambio legítimo de Run ID por Continue-As-New/retry con un segundo inicio independiente. Mantener aparte la identidad exacta usada para cancelar.

### Condición temporal y operacional

Mantener como hipótesis suficiente del estudio, **no como garantía publicada por Temporal ni prueba completa por sí sola**:

```text
t0   = primera autorización durable, anterior a cualquier RPC
Rmin = retención mínima efectivamente preservada
H    = horizonte máximo de autorización/envío desde t0
L    = cota demostrada hasta la decisión remota para TODOS los envíos,
       incluidos RPC antiguos, retries SDK y emisores suspendidos
m    = margen de reloj/operación

H + L + m < Rmin
```

No renovar `t0/notAfter` al reclamar, reiniciar, hacer retry u observar missing. Probar además preservación de identidad: borrado/reset/recreación, reducción de retención, restore y failover no pueden invalidar silenciosamente el perfil.

**Un timeout gRPC, AbortSignal, retry-count, percentil de latencia o comprobación local de fecha no demuestran `L`.** Un emisor puede suspenderse tras comprobar la fecha; una petición antigua puede llegar tarde. Archival no se admite como tombstone de deduplicación.

Sin cota y preservación justificadas para el perfil desplegado, el resultado es `observation_only`. Un test positivo dentro de retención no basta para habilitarlo.

### Tabla de decisión

| Observación y autoridad | Acción |
|---|---|
| Active + vínculo lógico y canonical compatibles | Adoptar/reconciliar; sin nuevo start. |
| Terminal + vínculo lógico verificado | Reconciliar resultado/compensación; no repetir trabajo. |
| Missing + unknown + canonical admisible + sin compensación + receipt vigente + perfil/ventana demostrados | Registrar autorización y reenviar el mismo inicio de forma acotada. Success/duplicate deben converger por la garantía remota. |
| Missing sin prueba, fuera de ventana o tras invalidación del perfil | Conservar unknown, observar con backoff y escalar. |
| Lectura/observación failed o unsupported | No nuevo envío ni conclusión definitiva. |
| Canonical terminal, cancel solicitado o compensación requerida | No redispatch; seguir observación/compensación existente. |
| Not-requested durable | Aplicar su lifecycle vigente; no confundir con un inicio previamente autorizado e incierto. |

Otra respuesta perdida tras el reenvío conserva unknown; no renueva la ventana ni convierte la segunda llamada en una ejecución nueva de negocio.

## Plan por fases y criterios de salida

### Fase A — Base segura: reutilizar lo integrado

#2678/#3506 entregaron ownership y observación conservadora. No repetir su implementación. Consumir su evidencia y preservar sus regresiones; cualquier drift posterior se comprueba antes de editar.

### Fase B — Prueba del perfil: parcialmente entregada

Reutilizar #3507 y `docs/evidence/ED-20261001-temporal-redispatch-profile-admission.md`. Su perfil probado es CLI v1.8.2 / Server 1.31.2, namespace local, retención 86400 s y SDK declarado 1.24.0. **Es evidencia de prueba, no certificación de producción.**

Pendiente: fijar el perfil realmente desplegado y demostrar cota de decisión remota, preservación de identidad y binding inmutable. Conservar el contraejemplo: incluso el requestId/payload originales pueden iniciar otra ejecución si se pierde la identidad retenida. Los tests de #3507 controlan orden previo al envío con colas sin workers; no equivalen a inyección de fallos arbitrarios de red.

Criterio de salida: perfil demostrable con límites y procedimiento de invalidación, o resultado explícito NO ADMITIDO. Este último preserva seguridad pero no satisface la aceptación positiva de redispatch.

### Fase C — Implementación acotada

Sólo tras admisión del diseño/perfil, extender la decisión y ejecución de efectos del reconciliador existente; persistir autorización, identidad y presupuesto en el intent; encapsular las garantías concretas en TemporalAdapter. Las comprobaciones de perfil y vinculación ausentes/inválidas deniegan por defecto.

No introducir otro provider ficticio para obtener un test verde. No cambiar la base conservadora en perfiles no admitidos.

### Fase D — Aceptación integral y operación

Prueba positiva sobre Engine/API + PostgreSQL + Temporal reales del perfil admitido, interleavings adversariales, invalidación y operación fuera de ventana. Revisión independiente sobre base/head exactos, CI/contratos/coverage/replay/arquitectura y Planning DB. No cerrar la issue por pruebas sólo de adapter ni por la aprobación de la dirección de diseño.

Si no se puede demostrar el perfil, volver a decisión explícita de producto/arquitectura. No sustituir automáticamente la aceptación por un workflow-manager permanente, Nexus, Signal/Update-With-Start o idempotencia de Activities: son alternativas del estudio con obligaciones y alcance distintos.

## Superficies a reutilizar

Rutas del corte #3506; refrescar consumidores y símbolos contra el HEAD de implementación antes de modificar:

| Responsabilidad | Superficies |
|---|---|
| Decisión y efectos | `packages/@dvt/engine/src/services/runMaintenance/decideStartRunIntentReconciliation.ts`, `StartRunIntentReconciliationPolicy.ts`, `StartRunIntentReconciliationEffects.ts` |
| Autorización, identidad y presupuesto | `packages/@dvt/engine/src/ports/IStartRunIntentStore.ts`, `src/domain/startRunIntentPolicy.ts`, `src/domain/startRunReconciliationPolicy.ts`, stores in-memory y `packages/@dvt/adapter-postgres/src/PostgresStartRunIntentStore.ts` / `PostgresStartRunIntentPersistence.ts` |
| Garantía/observación/transporte del provider | `packages/@dvt/engine/src/adapters/IProviderAdapter.ts`, `packages/@dvt/adapter-temporal/src/TemporalAdapter.ts`, `TemporalClient.ts` y wrappers afectados |
| Recovery honesto | `apps/api/src/application/services/recoverRunUseCase.ts`, `runStartDispatchResolver.ts` |
| Contrato, evidencia y operación | ADR-0030, StartRunProtocol, engine-policies, evidencia de admisión Temporal y riesgo ENG1 existentes |

Cada cambio debe justificarse; esta tabla no preautoriza tocar todos los ficheros. Sin migración/backfill/dual-read/dual-write o compatibilidad de historia técnica no publicada. Si el diseño cambia persistencia, conservar hard cut coordinado y disposición explícita de datos/efectos existentes; no resetear datos compartidos sin autorización.

## Pruebas obligatorias consolidadas

Se preservan las obligaciones originales y se precisan con los 14 escenarios del estudio:

1. Dos callers iniciales: una autorización; perdedor sin provider call, cancelación ni mutación ajena. Cubrir fresh no-estimado y prepared recovery.
2. Respuesta perdida con active: reenvío autorizado converge sin segunda cadena; duplicate se reconcilia con identidad verificada.
3. Ejecución cierra antes del reenvío dentro de retención: no se repite trabajo.
4. Missing temprano y llegada tardía del RPC original, ambos órdenes: no ausencia prematura ni cadena divergente.
5. Distinguir/capturar retries SDK frente a nuevas llamadas; contenido y presupuesto/horizonte total preservados.
6. Mismo ID con PlanRef/contexto distinto o receipt cross-tenant/cross-intent: rechazo sin adopción ni fuga.
7. Continue-As-New/retry legítimo frente a segunda cadena independiente; cancelación al execution ID correcto.
8. Reclaim/restart no renuevan ventana; receipts obsoletos y respuestas tardías no escriben ni cancelan indebidamente.
9. Emisor suspendido después de autorización y envío antiguo fuera del horizonte: demostrar protección o denegar admisión del perfil.
10. Expiración natural/borrado de history, incluso con requestId/payload originales: conservar contraejemplos, sin afirmar dedupe eterna.
11. Retención reducida, namespace recreado, restore/failover fuera del perfil: invalidación fail-closed; archival no acredita ausencia.
12. Failed/unsupported/sin garantía/canonical terminal/compensación: cero redispatch adicional; no falsos RunFailed/cancel; backoff y escalado durables/seleccionables sin hot loop.
13. Cancel aceptado con provider aún activo no resuelve; sólo confirmación suficiente cierra compensación. Terminal huérfano incompatible escala; recovery no aparenta confirmed mientras haya incertidumbre.
14. Medir por separado transmisiones RPC, cadenas, intentos de Activity y efectos persistidos. Reconciliación repetida idempotente y a lo sumo un evento canónico definitivo.

Las pruebas positivas del provider necesitan servicios reales/versiones fijadas; mocks sirven para interleavings internos, no para certificar deduplicación remota. Mantener RLS con rol no propietario, before/after durable y evidencia de no mutación. Telemetría de razones acotadas; sin receipts, secretos ni tenant/run/intent IDs en labels de alta cardinalidad.

## Definition of Ready del trabajo pendiente

- [x] Dirección de propuesta aprobada por Dunay: redispatch sólo condicionado a evidencia.
- [x] Base ownership/observación integrada mediante #3506; dependencia #2678 entregada.
- [x] Evidencia acotada de provider integrada mediante #3507, con límites explícitos.
- [ ] Consulta/admisión vigente de arquitectura y símbolos antes de nuevas modificaciones productivas.
- [ ] Perfil operativo, preservación de identidad, cota remota y binding justificados.
- [ ] Tabla de decisión y RED adversarial aceptados; solapamientos y HEAD refrescados.
- [ ] Plan de rollout/invalidación y revisión independiente identificados sin inventar asignaciones o consenso.

## Definition of Done — no rebajada

- [ ] Base de unknown durable, autoridad tipada, selección/restart y fencing preservada en el candidato final.
- [ ] Missing puntual y failed/unsupported nunca producen certeza prematura.
- [ ] Prueba positiva de redispatch seguro bajo perfil admitido, sin segunda cadena independiente y conservando identidad/contenido.
- [ ] Perfil no demostrado, vencido o invalidado no autoriza nuevo envío.
- [ ] Canonical terminal/compensación impiden adopción o reenvío indebidos; cancel request no equivale a confirmación.
- [ ] Backoff, presupuesto y escalado durables; no se renueva la ventana al recuperar.
- [ ] Recovery API y diagnósticos distinguen incertidumbre, confirmado, denegado y escalado.
- [ ] Un único aggregate/store/worker/rail por responsabilidad; no compatibilidad ni runtime paralelo.
- [ ] Engine/API/PostgreSQL/Temporal/coverage/replay/arquitectura/prepush y CI aplicables pasan sobre el SHA final, con omisiones declaradas.
- [ ] Diseño, perfil y verificación independiente del SHA final registrados; evidencia operacional correspondiente al despliegue, no inferida de un merge.

## Gobierno y revisión

GitHub conserva prioridad, estado y aceptación. Diseños existentes a consultar: `GH-2678-START-OWNERSHIP-PROTOCOL` y `GH-2679-REDISPATCH-PROFILE-ADMISSION`; no crear otro owner por actualizar la propuesta. Rails: `IWorkflowEngine.startRun`, `IRunMaintenanceService.reconcileOrphanedIntents` y `reconcileStartRunIntent`, más los consumidores API existentes.

En esta actualización se intentó `architecture-designs` con refresh deshabilitado: túnel indisponible. Sólo se reconcilian propuesta y evidencia de GitHub; no se declara nueva admisión ni mechanization, no se importa/reconstruye Planning DB y no se modifica código/configuración/despliegue.

Revisiones requeridas, sin afirmar participación: Dijkstra (linealización/ventana/interleavings), Ada (implementación/perfil/errores), Atila (hard cut y ausencia de bypass), Deming (prueba independiente real), Eisenhower (secuencia/operación) y Velázquez (estado observable y recovery honesto). ADR-0030/0031, StartRunProtocol y las reglas de contratos/ARC/preflight vigentes siguen siendo obligatorios.

- [Investigación completa y fuentes primarias](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/issues/2679#issuecomment-5926921272).
- [Base de ownership/observación integrada — #3506](https://github.com/dunay2/dvt/pull/3506).

Un intento lógico tiene un único owner vigente para dispatch y transiciones. No overload productivo sólo por ID ni compatibilidad token-free. El protocolo de despliegue/corte y el tratamiento de intents activos pertenecen a la entrega registrada; no se resetean datos por este saneo.

| `#5090` | **CLOSED 2026-11-12 — 12/12 children closed**; `#11086` and `#11641` both CLOSED, `#11642` landed via `#11660` | `#4333` storage-architecture owner only (P2, separate track) — **capstone `#11089` CLOSED 2026-11-12** | **1 open in beta (`#11089`) + 1 outside it (`#4333`)** |

**Stage 3 is days, not weeks — because the fixes are already written and switched off.** So (A) costs little and keeps the beta definition intact. **Still the owner's word to confirm, and nothing has been relabelled.**

### ⛔ AND THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS MORE THAN ANY OF THE ABOVE: **P1 grew 17 → 22 today**
```
P0 open: 10 (unchanged)   P1 open: **17 → 22**   issues closed today: 27 — of which only **2 were P0/P1**
6 NEW P1s filed today (#11641 #11642 #11646 #11653 #11654 #11656), all found by lanes doing real work
```
**"All P0/P1" is a moving target: the fleet is filing real Severe findings faster than it lands fixes.** That — not the size of any single wave — is the strongest reason to state an explicit **cut line** for the beta: a sha, a date, or a named issue set frozen at that moment. Otherwise the beta definition cannot be completed, only approached.

---

## STAGE 2 — ⏸ AFTER PRIVATE BETA, NOT IN IT: the venture-studio design partner

> **⛔ DO NOT LABEL `#2696` P0 OR P1 UNTIL THE PRIVATE-BETA SET IS COMPLETE, AND DO NOT DISPATCH IT.**
> The order is: **finish the private-beta set first.** A `P0`/`P1` label on this would make the automated harness pick it up and pull it into the beta wave — which is the opposite of the ruling. **It stays `P2-moderate`.** The ruling is: *"P2 for now, prioritise to P0 for the design partner after we complete the requirements for the private-beta"* (owner, 2026-11-09).
> **This section exists so the work is not lost, not so it is started.**

**The issue exists: `#2696` (currently `P2-moderate`) — "epic: meeting-ingestion pipeline for venture-builder customers — meeting-attunement".**
Its subject is exactly the partner's need: a meeting *is* a session, but its structure is different (speakers, agenda, decisions, action items, cross-meeting continuity) from an agent session's (tool calls, file edits, errors fixed).

**The question you raised — one universal extractor, or modular variants?** The evidence we have says **modularise the seam, keep one extractor**:
- The extractor is already staged S0→S6 (`#5087`) with a per-stage contract, and `#11484` derives the structural write vocabulary **per graph** from core + packs. That is already a per-domain configuration seam.
- A "meeting variant" that is a *prompt-and-vocabulary* variant costs little; a forked pipeline costs a second capstone and a second set of guarantees (verbatim retention `#10360`, value survival `#10989`).
- **So: one extractor, one proof, two profiles.** Stage 2's real work is (a) a meeting profile — speaker turns, decisions, action items — as a pack/vocabulary, and (b) the ingestion path from a transcript source to the extractor's door.

**This stage also carries `#2696` from P2 → the label that makes auto-dispatch pick it up *after* the beta set.** That relabel is part of the same decision as (A)/(B)/(C) above.

**⚠️ Prerequisite for iterating the profile at all — `#11661` (`P2-moderate`, deliberately NOT a beta item).** We record *which source version* produced a fact and never *which extractor* did, so after a profile change there is no way to tell which already-ingested meetings need re-extraction: every tuning round either re-extracts the whole corpus or silently serves output from a prompt that no longer exists, and neither failure is visible in the graph. Filed with its design — `extractorId` (a deliberately-bumped profile identity) + `extractorDigest` (a hash of the compiled prompt/vocabulary, for explainability), carried on the `extractedFrom` link exactly as `sourceVersion` already is, plus a third `unknown` state so pre-existing nodes are neither blessed as fresh nor re-extracted wholesale. **Do not pull it into the private-beta wave** — it is not a launch requirement. **Promote it to `P1` at the moment meeting-profile iteration starts**, because that is when its absence stops being a nuisance and becomes a correctness risk (`D13` draft → run → look → refine is the working method, so iteration starts immediately after stage 2 begins).

**The decision itself is recorded on `#2696` (comment `6752567775`) and `#11081` (`6752174448`, corrected by `6752335134`):** one extractor, no fork, meetings as connector #4 conforming to the registry-free mapper contract; the profile is a **shape** mapping (speaker turn · section · action item · decision · status update · blocker · open question), not a source-branded prompt set; no depth/cheap mode; no per-source field-cost registry.

## STAGE 3 — THE LONG-MEMORY FIXES THE BENCHMARK WOULD OTHERWISE MEASURE AS BROKEN

**The organising rule for this stage, and it is the whole point of it:** *an issue whose build landed is not done — it is at the "decide, or experiment and decide from the results" step.* **Building a retrieval improvement, leaving it switched off, and abandoning it is the worst outcome, and it is the current state of two of these.** Every row below therefore names its **decision home** and its **next action**, not just its subject.

| issue | state measured on `main` (2026-11-09) | next action | decision home |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#8488` (P1, **`owner-decision`**) | **lexical/BM25: LIVE** (on by default) · **context-enriched embeddings: implemented, `TORTOISE_CONTEXT_ENRICH` fail-safe OFF** | experiment (on/off on a fixed corpus, cost per chunk) → decide → per-category report | issue `#8488` + **lane `DECISION #8488`** (workspace `29C008AA`). ⭐ **Research appendix: `#8488` comment `6755095497`** (competitors, the quote-vs-paraphrase reconciliation, what we already ship) — **read before re-researching** |
| `#10538` (P1, **`owner-decision`** added 2026-11-09) | **fully implemented** in `tortoise/time_aware.py`; the dense-anchor branch is **`time_aware: bool = False`** | run `#9097`'s Q3 measurement over the expanded pipeline (`recall_all@5`, multi-session must move off **0.45**) → decide | issue `#10538` + the **same** lane as `#8488` (both flags decided together — deciding them apart yields a benchmark that measures neither) |
| `#2281` (P1) | built; both open children are **measurements** (`#9097`, `#11460`) | measurement only | issue `#2281` |
| `#2513` (P1, epic-scope) | scope unit 1 = `#10538`; re-injection `#10540` landed | **verify its three open children (below), then re-scope what is left** | issue `#2513` |

⚠️ **GAP CLOSED (2026-11-09).** `#8486`'s own gate ruling names **eight** issues as *"every open P0/P1/P2 we know affects this eval"*. Six were on this board; **`#2518`, `#2516`, `#2683`, `#2684`, `#8775` were missing entirely** and are added above, together with `#11682` (filed this session as `#8488` scope 1's delivery vehicle). `#11070` is the eighth and is **CLOSED**, so it needs no row. **The benchmark's precondition is now stated in one place** — it was previously enforced only by a comment on `#8486` and contradicted by silence here. See `#8488` comment `6754710803` for the evidence.


**⛔ PRIORITY — these six stay `P2` on purpose, and this is the rule (owner, 2026-11-09 / 2026-11-10).** *"P1 would mean making it a requirement before we launch the private beta."* **None of these are beta requirements.** They are Stage 3 — **after** the private-beta set is merged and closed, **before** the benchmark runs. Their wave is carried by this row, not by a priority label.

**They may be re-prioritised to `P1` once the private-beta set is complete**, if the owner then decides they are needed. Until that point a `P1` label on any of them would make the automated harness pull it into the beta wave — which is exactly what Stage 2's `⛔ DO NOT LABEL` rule exists to prevent for `#2696`. **Leave them `P2`; re-prioritise after beta, not before.**

⚠️ **CONSEQUENCE TO RESOLVE — `#11682` is currently `P1-severe`.** By this board's own definition (*"beta ships when the open `P0-blocker` + `P1-severe` issues are merged and closed"*) that makes it **beta work**, which contradicts the owner's stated intent for this work. **Flagged for the owner's call: leave `P1` and treat the composer as a beta requirement, or drop it to `P2` and let this Stage 3 row sequence it.** Not changed by this edit — relabelling is the owner's.

### `#2513`'s three open children — **unlabelled, and NOT previously tracked here. That was a gap in this board.**
| issue | subject | current labels | **proposed** |
|---|---|---|---|
| `#11382` | the seed key is stripped and the graph group key is racy on the session-re-injection path | **none** (a merged PR `#11365` references it — so the fix may have landed) | **`P1-severe`**, Stage 3 |
| `#10819` | the census window is not narrowed on the R6 rerank DEGRADE arms | **none** (merged `#11212` references it) | **`P2-moderate`**, Stage 3 |
| `#8713` | the C4 re-injection arm's pre-registered surface census is **falsified** | `complexity:standard`, `team:epistemic-team` — **no P** | **`P2-moderate`**, Stage 3 |

⚠️ **All three have zero comments and merged PRs that reference them — the "fix landed, issue never closed" pattern.** Their first step is therefore **verification, not coding**: a lane confirms whether the merged work addressed each, then closes or re-scopes it. **The proposed labels above await the owner's approval; nothing has been applied.**

**These are the ones we already know are broken and know how they are broken.** Running LongMemEval before them measures our own known defects.

## STAGE 4 — THE BENCHMARKS
| what | issue | state |
|---|---|---|
| LongMemEval-S (end-to-end QA) | `#8486` | **never executed** — no comparable number exists |
| the ask exit measurement | `#9097` (+ `#11460` re-registration) | pre-registration owed |
| **reasoning (gbrain)** | `#1402` epic agent-reasoning eval battery · `#2080` epic gbrain learnings · `#2107` capstone | partially set up |
| battery wiring | `#2800`, `#11056` | in progress |

**Rule for this stage: a benchmark result is only published with (a) the sha, (b) the corpus hash, and (c) the profile/config it ran under.** A number without those three is not a measurement.

---

## Working rules (learned the hard way; all measured)

- **One lane per item; the terminal milestone is LANDED + CLOSED**, not "a PR opened".
- **Closure requires proven criteria** — a closing keyword only when the last criterion is proven beside the measurement.
- **A review lane records at the FINAL head.** Push first, then review, then record, then **read back** `~/.pi/agent/reviews/…json` and assert `head_sha` matches. A record bound to a stale sha is indistinguishable from no record — three died that way on 2026-11-09.
- **`mergeable` AND `mergeStateStatus` are both caches.** `git merge-tree --write-tree origin/main <head>` is the only authority; acting on a phantom `DIRTY` moves heads and destroys reviews.
- **Never edit a PR body after a review is recorded** — it wipes the attestation.
- **Never push to a PR whose CI is queued or running** — it cancels that run.
- **Pre-flight before dispatch**: `collision_preflight.py <N>` + `who-is-on.sh <N>`.
- **Keep advanced work.** Adopt and drive existing work to completion; re-do only where it is genuinely off, and file a follow-up rather than starting over silently.

## Instruments (do not re-derive)
`~/.pi/agent/state/P01-PRMAP.md` · `~/.pi/agent/state/WORKSTATUS.md` · `uv run python tools/surface-target-check.py` · `tools/surface_manifest.py check` · the `tracking-table` comment this issue carries (posted every beat).

items.title: Supervised overnight sessions: trial notes, state and next step (not a skill yet)
items.body:
## Why

On 2026-09-29/30 the owner and a direction session (codex-skills-92) ran several Claude Code sessions overnight to use spare quota. The direction session supervised them. The owner wants to keep this pattern and run more trials, but **not** turn it into a skill yet. This issue holds the pattern, what the trial taught, and where the next session starts, so none of it depends on one conversation.

## The pattern, as trialed

1. **One brief per session, one repository.** Say what the session may do (merge, deploy or not), the stop points, and where to ask. Never widen a brief afterwards; a peer message can't.
2. **Owner questions go on the issue,** as a comment starting "Owner question:". The session then continues with other work, and a reply from the `cbusillo` account is the answer.
3. **A supervisor check every ~23 minutes** (a session-only cron in the direction session). It writes a ledger of session, repository, issue and tab title, nudges stalled sessions with the exact facts, gathers open owner questions, and posts one short status line to the owner's Discord thread. It never decides for the owner.
4. **Land through the train with the maintained `launchplane-train-drive.py`** (#880, #882), never with hand-written loops.

## What it showed

- **It worked:** 86 PRs merged across 24 repositories and 21 issues closed between 01:30 and 12:15 UTC. The OPW testing milestone ran out of agent work. The check caught four silent stalls that the sessions themselves missed. Sessions correctly refused bad input: work outside their brief, and a label that would have wedged the train.
- **Lessons:**
  - The supervisor widened briefs twice; it shouldn't.
  - One case-sensitivity bug turned into six rounds on the train until a full sweep. When a bug fits a pattern, check the whole path.
  - `git stash` is shared across worktrees, so sessions shouldn't use it.
  - The shared CI runners saturated for hours.
  - Relayed decisions: sessions whose brief only trusts replies from `cbusillo` won't act on the bot's "Owner decision" comments. Either the brief accepts decisions from the direction session, or the owner types a line in that session.
  - Copy-pasted `!` shell lines misfired and posted duplicates. Answering in plain words and letting the direction session record the decision worked better.
  - Reusing old sessions caused most of the friction. **Start a fresh tab per task instead** (launcher notes on cbusillo/discord-blue#164).

## Owner decisions from the trial

- Sessions the supervisor launches overnight start **without** the Discord channels flag, so there's no blocking prompt; the supervisor watches them. Sessions the owner starts keep the flag.
- A daily "needs you" digest in Discord is worth trying, not committed. `shiny-code-app[bot]` email goes to Trash for now.

## State at hand-off (2026-09-30, about 13:30 UTC)

Still running, each on its own brief:
- **launchplane-9f** (tab "PR 2601 review"): landing the green Dependabot PRs. sellyouroutboard#262 (major version) is held, and sellyouroutboard#265 and verireel#393 are being diagnosed.
- **launchplane-41** (tab "Go Product repos Launchplane call"): landing cbusillo/launchplane#2653, which makes #2605's deploys run.
- **mediaforce-78**: mediaforce#633 slice 2, plus closing #585.
- **MCR session** (new tab, the first one started by the launcher): media-control-relay#1, landing #119 and then building a Developer ID release candidate for the owner's hands-on TV test.

Open follow-ups:
- cbusillo/discord-blue#164: reach Codex sessions from a supervising session (the next test).
- cbusillo/discord-blue#165: raw tags in Discord threads (example link recorded).
- cbusillo/context-panel#719: show all OpenAI and Anthropic accounts; build it as a Sol 6.1 vs Astra comparison.
- #883: the train driver treats a held lease as failure during a long landing.
- cbusillo/launchplane#2639, #2650, #2652: train gaps found overnight.
- cbusillo/jetbrains-inspection-api#433: PyCharm can't open worktrees. There are two causes, and a comment records both.

**Time-sensitive:** all three OpenAI accounts have resets expiring **2026-10-03**, plus 3–4 more within 30 days (see `shiny-infra-ops/docs/reference/capacity.md`).

## Next action

Start a fresh direction session in `~/Developer/codex-skills` with: `/shared:direction Daily turn, then pick up codex-skills#884: test starting Codex sessions from the direction session (discord-blue#164), aiming to use the Oct 3 OpenAI resets on context-panel#719 (Sol 6.1 vs Astra).` Check the four running sessions above first; each should have finished or be close.

items.title: PRD: multi-environment semantic layer — connection groups

milestone.title: 1.4.4 — Multi-environment semantic layer
milestone.description: Connection groups foundation + per-environment semantic layer scoping. Spawned from audit #2329 + PRD #2336. Lets a single workspace point a single semantic layer at multiple connections (dev/staging/prod, US/EU/APAC), with group-scoped content (entities, dashboards, scheduled tasks, approvals, PII, prompts) and atomic publish extension.

items.body:
> **Drafted from the audit in [#2329](https://github.com/AtlasDevHQ/atlas/issues/2329)** — see [`.claude/research/multi-env-semantic-layer.md`](../blob/main/.claude/research/multi-env-semantic-layer.md) for the full surface map and the option comparison this PRD is anchored on. Defaults below were picked without a live interview (background session, "no stopping" directive); items marked **⚠️ confirm** are the highest-leverage assumptions worth a redirect before implementation starts.

## Problem Statement

I run Atlas against three regional Postgres replicas (us-int, eu, apac) that share the same schema. Today, every connection-scoped row in Atlas's internal database — semantic entities, scheduled tasks, dashboard cards, PII classifications, approvals — duplicates per connection. My `/admin/semantic` page shows three "accounts" entities. My PII scan ran three times to classify the same column three ways. A schema change to my `orders` metric needs me to edit it in three places, or I have to remember to use a NULL `connection_id` (which works for entities but doesn't extend to the rest of the surface).

The fragility goes deeper than UX. Migration 0028 cost us+apac a prod boot because `connection_id` was baked into the natural key of `semantic_entities` and a schema evolution broke uniqueness across `entity_type`. The connection-scoped uniqueness model has *already* been the proximate cause of a prod incident.

Same shape will hit any customer with multi-region prod, staging + prod side-by-side, or per-tenant schema copies. The dogfood pain is the canary.

## Solution

Introduce a **connection group** — a named bundle of connections that share a logical schema (e.g. "prod" containing us-int + eu + apac). Connection-scoped content moves from `connection_id` to `connection_group_id`. A multi-region org with one shared schema has one group with three members; semantic entities, scheduled tasks, dashboard cards, approvals, and PII classifications live on the group, not on individual members.

At query time, a conversation still picks one connection to *execute* against — the group is the *content scope*, the connection is the *execution target*. Operators see one entity, one PII classification, one dashboard card. Publish promotes drafts across the whole group atomically.

For backward compatibility, every existing connection is backfilled into a single-member group on its own (1:1). Orgs with one connection see zero behavior change. Multi-region orgs merge their connections into a group via one explicit admin action.

UI surface uses the word **"environment"** (familiar to anyone with dbt/Terraform/Vercel experience); the schema and code use **`connection_group`** (precise, no overload with deploy-mode "environment"). Documentation calls a group "an environment" in the same paragraph it explains "this is the unit of content sharing."

## User Stories

1. As a multi-region operator, I want my YAML entities to appear once in `/admin/semantic`, so that I don't have to mentally deduplicate three rows for every metric.
2. As a multi-region operator, I want to edit an entity definition once and have the change apply to every region, so that I'm not maintaining three forks of the same metric.
3. As a multi-region operator, I want to publish a draft entity change once and have it promote across all members of the group atomically, so that no region briefly serves stale semantic layer.
4. As a multi-region operator, I want my PII column classifications to be group-wide, so that the privacy scan runs once and the audit story is unified.
5. As a multi-region operator, I want a single dashboard card to render against my chosen group member, so that my "Weekly Revenue" dashboard isn't triplicated.
6. As a multi-region operator, I want my scheduled tasks to belong to a group with a chosen executing member, so that "send daily orders report" doesn't fire three times.
7. As a multi-region operator, I want one approval queue entry per query (not per region), so that an approval covers any group member running the same SQL.
8. As an admin, I want to merge existing connections into a connection group via one admin action, so that I can collapse pre-group duplication without manual SQL.
9. As an admin, I want to split a group back into individual connections (or move a member to a different group), so that I can react when one region's schema diverges from the others.
10. As an admin, I want my single-connection org to keep working with zero changes, so that I don't pay a tax for a feature I don't need.
11. As a frontline analyst chatting with Atlas, I want my conversation to know which environment it executes against, so that "EU sales" runs on the EU connection without me re-specifying every turn.
12. As a frontline analyst, I want to override the execution target for one query (e.g. "run this on us-int instead"), so that I can compare regions ad-hoc without starting a new conversation.
13. As a frontline analyst, I want the connection picker in the chat header to show "EU (prod environment)" instead of three separate "EU" / "US" / "APAC" entries with no context, so that I understand the group structure.
14. As a developer using `@useatlas/sdk`, I want a clear major-version migration path from `connectionId` to `connectionGroupId` in response shapes, so that my SDK upgrade is predictable.
15. As a developer using `@useatlas/sdk`, I want the SDK to expose group members so I can render a "running on us-int" indicator in my embedded chat, so that my end users have execution-target visibility.
16. As an Atlas operator inheriting this from a fresh deploy, I want the default behavior (one group per connection) to be invisible — no banners, no setup prompts, so that the feature is zero-cost until I need it.
17. As a security reviewer, I want the SQL whitelist to enforce that an entity is only queryable on connections whose group owns it, so that cross-group leaks are impossible at the validation layer.
18. As a developer writing custom plugins, I want connection-group context exposed in tool execution so my plugin tool can pick the right execution target, so that plugins compose with the group model.
19. As an admin auditing draft history, I want to see "drafted, applied to prod group" rather than "drafted on us-int, drafted on eu, drafted on apac (3 entries)", so that the audit log reflects the logical change, not the physical replicas.
20. As an admin viewing `/admin/connections`, I want each connection card to show its group membership, so that I can see fleet structure at a glance.
21. As an admin, I want to rename a group ("prod" → "production") without breaking existing references, so that group names are mutable display labels, not foreign keys.
22. As an admin reading the docs, I want the term "environment" to be used consistently in UI copy and to map to the term "connection group" in the API/schema, so that I can move between docs and code without re-learning.
23. As a 1.4.x → 1.6.x upgrader, I want the migration to be idempotent and recoverable, so that I can re-run it if a previous attempt failed mid-transaction.
24. As an operator concerned about the 0028-class boot crash, I want the new natural-key change to ship with the same real-Postgres migration smoke test that catches missing-column-in-unique-index bugs, so that this refactor doesn't re-introduce a boot regression.
25. As an admin in developer/draft mode, I want the pending-changes banner to show "12 draft changes (across 3 environments)" with a drill-down that groups by entity, not by environment, so that I see the logical work, not the multiplicative spread.

## Implementation Decisions

**Primary model: Option A — Connection Groups.** Audit recommendation; smallest migration cost; mode-system extension is mechanical. Option B (template + environments) is the documented fallback if interview surfaces per-env override requirements that Option A can't model.

### New module — `connection_groups`

- Internal-DB table: `connection_groups` keyed by `(id, org_id, name, created_at, updated_at)`.
- New column on `connections`: `group_id` referencing `connection_groups(id)`. Nullable during transition; backfilled non-null post-migration.
- Backfill strategy: one group per existing connection, group name = connection name. 1:1 mapping. Existing single-connection orgs are unaffected.
- The migration is added to `MANAGED_AUTH_MIGRATIONS` if it touches Better Auth tables (it doesn't — no concern). Smoke test via `migrate-pg.test.ts`.

### Schema deltas to existing tables

The six audited tables migrate `connection_id` → `connection_group_id`. For each:

- `semantic_entities` — Replace `connection_id` with `connection_group_id` in body and in the three partial unique indexes. Natural key becomes `(org_id, entity_type, name, COALESCE(connection_group_id, '__default__'))` per status. The COALESCE NULL-safety pattern is preserved.
- `dashboard_cards` — `connection_id` → `connection_group_id`. **⚠️ confirm** card execution: picks the group's "primary" member at view time vs. shows all members side-by-side. Default pick: primary member. Future "side-by-side" mode is a follow-on issue.
- `conversations` — Keep `connection_id` (execution target) **and** add `connection_group_id` (content scope). These are decoupled. The conversation picks one group member to execute against, but reads semantic entities scoped to the group.
- `scheduled_tasks` — `connection_id` → `connection_group_id`. Task picks "primary" group member at fire time. **⚠️ confirm** federation: should a task run on every member or just one? Default pick: one (the primary). Federation is a follow-on.
- `approval_queue` — `connection_id` → `connection_group_id`. Drop the `DEFAULT 'default'` (it was vestigial). One approval covers any group member running the same query. **⚠️ confirm**.
- `pii_column_classifications` — `connection_id` → `connection_group_id`. Drop the `DEFAULT 'default'`. The `UNIQUE(org_id, table_name, column_name, ...)` index migrates to use `connection_group_id`. **⚠️ confirm** — assumes all group members share the same schema; same column = same PII tag.

### Content mode + atomic publish

- The publish transaction (`/api/v1/admin/publish`) extends to operate on `connection_group_id` keys. The transaction stays atomic across all six tables.
- Phase 4 cascade (archive-on-connection-archive) becomes "archive-on-group-archive." Archiving a single group member does **not** archive content. Archiving a group archives all content.
- Mode-system `tables.ts` registry updates: `semantic_entities` keying changes from `connection_id` to `connection_group_id` in `readFilter` / `resolveStatusClause`.

### Whitelist / SQL validation

- The whitelist (`packages/api/src/lib/semantic/whitelist.ts`) keys entities by group, not connection. A query executed on connection C resolves the entity through C's group. If C is moved to a different group, the whitelist re-resolves on next query.
- New invariant: an entity is queryable on connection C iff C's group owns the entity (or C has no group, legacy single-connection orgs).

## Testing Decisions

A good test for this feature targets **external behavior** — admin sees one entity not three; published draft promotes across all members; conversation routing picks the right member — and avoids asserting on the COALESCE sentinel or internal SQL shape.

**Modules with new unit tests:**

- `withGroupScope` deep module — pure unit tests for query-builder composition. No DB. Test the boundary cases: null group_id (legacy), missing group, group with zero members, group with one member.
- `connection_groups` CRUD service — unit tests with `createConnectionTestLayer`. Test create / rename / delete-with-content / move-member / archive cascade.
- Group-aware whitelist resolution — unit test the invariant that "entity queryable on C iff C's group owns it."

**Modules with new integration tests:**

- Migration smoke (`migrate-pg.test.ts`) — extends the real-Postgres smoke to cover the schema change. Catches missing-column-in-unique-index bugs (the 0028 class). This is **required**, not optional.
- Atomic publish transaction — uses Effect test layers (`buildTestLayer`). Test the multi-table publish across a group with 3 members; assert rollback on partial failure (one table fails → all roll back).
- Mode-system draft counts — assert the banner shows one count per logical entity, not multiplied by group size.

**Modules with browser e2e (`e2e/browser/`):**

- Multi-region admin happy path. Tagged `@llm`. New `multi-env-admin.test.ts` mirrors the `published-vs-draft.test.ts` pattern (it already covers mode-system flows on a single-connection setup; this extends to a group).
- Conversation-with-group-context. Tagged `@llm`. Verifies the chat header's "environment / member" combobox renders correctly and per-turn overrides work.

**Test prior art:**

- `packages/api/src/lib/db/__tests__/migrate-pg.test.ts` — real-Postgres migration smoke; this is the gate.
- `packages/api/src/lib/semantic/__tests__/overlay-queries-integration.test.ts` — closest existing test for connection-scoped entity reads. New tests follow this shape but key on `connection_group_id`.
- `packages/api/src/api/__tests__/admin-publish.test.ts` — atomic publish transaction tests. New tests extend the matrix to include group-scoped tables.
- `packages/web/e2e/browser/published-vs-draft.test.ts` — pattern for content-mode browser e2e.

## Out of Scope

- **Cross-group query federation.** Running one query against all members of a group and merging results. Real feature, real customer ask, separate problem — touches data residency and result-set merging semantics. Defer to follow-on.
- **Per-environment entity overrides.** If an entity definition needs to differ per group member, the model needed is Option B (templates + environments). v1 ships Option A only; if the post-launch interview surfaces this need, escalate to a v2 PRD.
- **Auto-detect routing.** Inferring the right group member from query content ("show me EU sales" → eu connection). Possible future; not in v1.
- **Vocabulary alternatives.** "Workspace" / "target" / "fleet" / "stage" all rejected in this PRD's "Vocabulary" decision. Out of scope to relitigate.
- **Sandbox / sidecar changes.** The execution layer is unchanged; only content scoping moves.
- **Plugin schema changes.** Plugins already receive `connectionId` in tool execution context; that continues to work. Adding `connectionGroupId` to plugin context is a follow-on (user story 18).
- **Schema-fingerprint heuristic for merge prompts.** "Hey, your 3 connections look identical — merge them?" UX is appealing but error-prone. v1 ships admin-initiated merge only.
- **Deprecating the `default` sentinel in `approval_queue` / `pii_column_classifications`.** Dropping the column default value is part of this PRD; deprecating the sentinel string everywhere is out of scope.
